summary: A sound paper with realistic situations and good distractors in Parts 1-3. All answer keys are correct and appear in question order. Part 1 (533 words) and Part 4 (653 words) are on the short side, and the Part 4 notes repeat the lecture's words closely, so the last section is a little easier than a real Part 4.
strengths: Part 1 has proper corrections: Swallow vs Heron Cottage, the 12th already booked so the 19th, the old website price 580 vs 640, Sunday vs Monday closing, the satnav's wrong turn at the church.
Part 2 MCQs mention every option and rule two out (bus depot and street market; fire ten years ago and staff shortage denied).
The Part 2 matching box has two strong distractors (stored until prices improve - explicitly denied; not accepted - used for mattresses).
Part 3 is a natural supervisor-student discussion in which most wrong options are raised and rejected.

issues.problem: Part 1 script is 533 words, under the usual 600+ for a real Part 1, so it runs short on the recording.
issues.change: Part 1 extended to real length with natural exchanges and distractors (answers unchanged) and re-recorded with ElevenLabs, 2026-11-10.

issues.problem: Part 4 (653 words) is short and its notes copy the lecture almost word for word (e.g. 'high mountains and wide ___' / 'high mountain passes and wide deserts', 'state ___' / 'state secret'). There is almost no paraphrase or distractor, which makes Part 4 easier than in the real test.
issues.change: Notes reworded away from the lecture (earlier fix); Part 4 extended to about 785 words with distractors (answers unchanged) and re-recorded with ElevenLabs, 2026-11-10.

issues.problem: Q2 'Heron' is not spelled out; it relies on 'as in the bird'. Fine for a common word, but real Part 1 tests usually spell unusual names.
